newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac says France must go further with tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Chirac says France must go further with tax cuts.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Thursday that the government had taken a first step in cutting taxes but that it had to go further and as soon as possible.

"The state has taken a first step on cutting taxes. It must go further, especially on income tax," he said in a television interview. Asked how fast, Chirac replied "as soon as possible", but that it was for the government to decide.
Chirac also reiterated his line that "draconian" cuts in public spending were needed.

The French 1997 budget, unveiled in September, includes 25 billion francs ($5 billion) of income tax cuts to take effect next year as the first step in a five-year package of income tax cuts worth 75 billion French francs ($15 billion) in total.
